25023.notes: Massachusetts tax titles are MUNICIPAL, not county-run. Plymouth County cities/towns (Brockton, Plymouth, Hingham, Lakeville, etc.) each run their own tax taking/sale or assignment under M.G.L. c. 60. After tax title attaches, foreclosure of the right of redemption is typically via Massachusetts Land Court. Brockton and Town of Plymouth are large examples only — always research the specific municipality. Post-Tyler excess-proceeds scrutiny is active statewide.
25023.auctionFormat: Varies by municipality (in-person or online public auction / tax title assignment)

auctionPlatform.label: Municipal treasurer/collector (example: Town of Plymouth Treasurer-Collector; some towns use Bid4Assets)

25023.auctionFrequency: Periodically, as each city/town schedules tax sales, assignment auctions, or post–Land Court possession auctions
25023.depositRules: Set by each municipality’s tax collector/treasurer for that sale notice — no single county rule. Confirm deposit, certified funds, buyer’s premium, and registration with the specific town (Hingham and Lakeville examples have used public auction deposits and buyer premiums).

taxCollector.label: City/town Treasurer-Collector (Plymouth County has no county tax-sale office)

clerkOfCourt.label: Plymouth County Registry of Deeds + Massachusetts Land Court for foreclosure

propertyAppraiser.label: Municipal assessor for the specific city/town (no single county appraiser)

25023.survivingLiens: Tax title / Land Court foreclosure process. Federal liens and some municipal betterments can survive. Verify water/sewer and local betterment liens with the municipality before bidding.
25023.quietTitle: Land Court foreclosure of the right of redemption is the standard path to marketable title after a tax taking/sale — that proceeding is effectively required, not optional.

27123.notes: Minnesota tax-deed (forfeiture) system — not a lien certificate sale. After statutory forfeiture to the State of Minnesota for unpaid taxes, Ramsey County Productive Properties (formerly Tax-Forfeited Land) appraises parcels and offers them at public auction, typically online via MNBid (mnbid.mn.gov). Minimum bid is appraised value; full payment required (no contract-for-deed on recent auctions). Most private liens/mortgages are canceled at forfeiture; federal/state tax liens can survive. Spring 2026 online auction referenced on county site; residential sales often restricted to owner-occupancy/noncommercial use — verify terms per sale.

27123.depositRules: Register on MNBid. On award, payment of the full winning bid is typically due within ~14 business days by cashier’s check/money order to Surplus Services (per auction FAQ). No contract-for-deed; failure to pay voids award. Confirm current deposit/award terms on the live auction listing.

51153.notes: Virginia judicial tax-deed sales via Special Commissioner. Prince William County Tax Administration refers long-delinquent accounts (typically after Dec 31 of second anniversary of delinquency; sooner for blight/nuisance/low-value) to Taxing Authority Consulting Services (TACS) for Circuit Court foreclosure and public auction. Auctions may be in-person/simulcast (Dr. A.J. Ferlazzo Building, Woodbridge) or online-only (e.g. bidding closing July 13, 2026 cycle). Judicial sale generally conveys free and clear of liens including taxes when court-confirmed; non-judicial sales for limited parcel types use special warranty deeds.

51153.depositRules: Terms vary by sale notice: typically register with auctioneer for online bidding; day-of deposit percentage of bid in certified funds for in-person; court confirmation required before deed on judicial sales. Bidders may not owe delinquent taxes to Prince William County. Review each sale’s general terms package.

25013.notes: Massachusetts tax titles are MUNICIPAL, not county-run. Hampden County cities/towns (Springfield, Westfield, Chicopee, Holyoke, etc.) each run their own tax taking/sale or assignment under M.G.L. c. 60. City of Springfield maintains tax title lists and has used public auctions for collector’s deeds/assignments; Land Court foreclosure of the right of redemption is the path to marketable title. Always research the specific municipality. Post-Tyler excess-proceeds scrutiny is active statewide.
